verdict: Nike's revenue rose 1% to $11.7B — wholesale grew 7% and North America 4%, but Nike Direct fell 4% and Greater China 9% — and lower selling prices plus higher tariffs cut the gross margin by three points, dropping profit 31% to $727M.

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: down from 45.4%, on discounts and higher tariffs

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Nike's home market — wholesale demand led, with apparel up 11% and footwear flat.

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: Europe, the Middle East and Africa — up 6% on reported numbers, up 1% without currency help.

segments.name: Asia Pacific & Latin America
segments.note: Asia-Pacific (outside Greater China) and Latin America.

segments.name: Greater China
segments.note: China — down 9% (-10% without currency help) as footwear fell 11%.

segments.name: Converse
segments.note: The Converse sneaker brand — down across all territories.

segments.name: Global Brand & Corporate
segments.note: Global brand divisions plus corporate leftovers (mostly currency-hedge results).

opex.name: Demand creation
opex.note: Advertising and sports marketing — down 3%, with lower brand marketing after last year's big sports events.

opex.name: Operating overhead
opex.note: Salaries, technology and running the business — flat YoY, as higher wage costs were offset by lower administrative costs.

takeaways.title: Wholesale carried the quarter
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 1% to $11.7B (down 1% without currency help). Wholesale revenue grew 7% and North America 4%, but Nike Direct fell 4% — digital sales dropped 12% — and Greater China fell 9%.

takeaways.title: Discounts and tariffs squeezed the margin
takeaways.text: Gross margin fell 320 basis points to 42.2%, mainly on lower average selling prices — higher discounts and channel mix — plus higher tariffs in North America. Inventories were $8.1B, down 2%.

takeaways.title: Profit fell 31%
takeaways.text: Net income fell 31% to $727M and EPS to $0.49. Selling and administrative expense fell 1% to $4.0B — demand creation down 3% and overhead flat — but not enough to offset the margin squeeze.

otherDetail: $18M of net interest income, less $23M of other expense, net.
footerNote: Segment revenues are Nike's divisional revenues; 'Global Brand & Corporate' combines Global Brand Divisions ($9M) and Corporate (-$8M, mostly currency-hedge results).
